note: International source-linked briefings. Coach-voice takes are editorial drafts for review, not quotations or claims of the coach's personal experiences.

items.title: The Elite Series heads from Hamburg to Bangkok, Las Vegas and Lyon
items.summary: The official 2026/27 schedule opens in Hamburg on 30–31 October, followed by London, Bangkok, Las Vegas and Lyon. Elite 15 and Challenger 15 races share the stage on the road to Hong Kong 2027.
items.take: Keep the lesson simple: look for a repeatable pace and clean transitions rather than copying every elite detail.

items.title: Singapore, Melbourne and Hong Kong offer an overseas start line
items.summary: The official calendar lists Singapore on 26–29 November, Melbourne on 9–13 December and Hong Kong on 7–10 January. An away race also means planning travel, sleep and recovery.
items.take: Make the weekend practical. Sort sleep, familiar food and the venue journey before adding anything complicated.

items.title: Stockholm: Australia defends its mixed-relay world title
items.summary: PUMA's World Championships report records Australia's mixed-relay win in 50:19, with Jess Pettrow on the title-defending team. Joanna Wietrzyk also finished second in the women's Elite 15 solo race.
items.take: Know your role and communicate it clearly. A good shared plan makes race-day decisions simpler.

items.title: Elite qualification switches to a rolling points system
items.summary: HYROX's new framework uses a rolling 365-day window: the best five singles results or best three doubles results count. Elite Series doubles partners must share the same nationality and an active athlete licence is required.
items.take: Check what counts, then choose a season you can prepare for. More races are not automatically better.

items.title: Hong Kong to host the 2027 World Championships
items.summary: HYROX announced the first World Championships in the Asia-Pacific region, at Hong Kong's AsiaWorld-Expo on 10–13 June 2027. Qualification gives the season a clear international destination.
items.take: Turn the ambition into a clear next step. Training should be simple to understand and practical to carry out.

items.title: Project Podium opens a new route to athlete support
items.summary: PUMA announced a programme offering men's, women's and adaptive solo podium finishers at the 2026 World Championships the opportunity to become PUMA athletes for the following season, with kit, resources and performance support.
items.take: New opportunities are positive. Keep the next training decision focused on what will genuinely help you progress.
